diagnosis.summary: Checkout‑api latency spiked after the 10:15 deployment of v4.17, causing connection‑pool exhaustion and 504 timeouts. The issue resolved immediately when the service was rolled back to v4.16.
diagnosis.root_cause: The upgrade to orders‑client v3 reduced the database pool from 50 to 10 connections with a 2000 ms acquire timeout, exhausting the pool during checkout requests.

evidence.finding: Commit a91f3c2 changed orders‑client to v3, setting pool.max_connections from 50 to 10 and acquire_timeout_ms to 2000.
p95 latency jumped from 200 ms to 2150 ms within minutes of the deployment.
At 10:40, pool max=10, in_use=10, waiting=143, acquire_timeout_ms≈1800, with 212 timeouts per minute.
212 ERRORs in last 15 min reporting ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and checkout 504 after 2500 ms.
Slowest trace shows a 1829 ms db.pool.acquire span during checkout.

ruled_out: Payment gateway outage – authorize spans complete in ~187 ms.
Load spike unrelated to deployment – latency and pool exhaustion began exactly at deployment time.

proposal.rationale: The latency spike and connection‑pool exhaustion began immediately after the 10:15 deployment of v4.17, which introduced a reduced orders‑client pool (10 connections). Rolling back to the previous stable release v4.16 restores the original pool size and resolves the 504 timeouts.
